change.title: pr-80528-flat
change.description: ref(crons): Reorganize incident creation / issue occurrence logic
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Monitor context returns the raw config, so the `schedule_type` display label is never used
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` makes a copy of the config at line 160 and puts the display label for `schedule_type` into that copy at line 162. Line 168 then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the copy, so the copy is thrown away and the event's monitor context still carries the integer `schedule_type`. The bug already existed and the move kept it as it was. Since the function now lives in its own module, this is an easy place to fix it: `"config": config,`. The serializer does the same transformation and uses its copy correctly (`src/sentry/monitors/serializers.py:240-242`).

contracts.action: mark_failed now delegates to try_incident_threshold (moved from mark_failed_threshold)
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed mark_failed_threshold in mark_failed.py at base
contracts.before_after: The body is identical to the removed function. It still sets status=ERROR, does get_or_create on the incident, produces occurrences when the monitor is not muted, and sends the monitor_environment_failed signal. No other callers or mock.patch targets referenced the removed names (mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, get_failure_reason, SimpleCheckIn in mark_failed); the only matches for create_issue_platform_occurrence are the separate uptime function.
contracts.visible_effect: No change to the issues or occurrences that get produced.
contracts.failure_mode: Unchanged from before: exceptions propagate to the callers (consumer and clock tasks) just as they did.

summary: This PR is a straight move of code. `mark_failed_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence` and their helpers move to `logic/incidents.py` (as `try_incident_threshold`) and `logic/incident_occurrence.py` (as `create_incident_occurrence`). `SimpleCheckIn` moves to `monitors/types.py`. The function bodies are unchanged, and no other code or test imports or patches the old names. The one note is a bug the move kept as it was: the monitor context returns the raw config, not the copy that has the `schedule_type` display label.
